rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this table pushes obfuscation moderately higher while protecting the program's hot numeric loops (loop_unroll, simple_types, stepanov kernels dominate runtime). SUB gets the highest weights since arithmetic substitution is cheap, always applicable in these integer-heavy kernels, and composes well with other passes; FLA stays fairly high because control-flow flattening yields strong static-analysis resistance and the benchmark's largest functions (main, introsort instantiations) benefit most, but its RuntimeCost weight is kept below SUB to limit flattening of tight inner loops. BCF is mid-range: opaque predicates add real analysis friction but their per-branch overhead argues against aggressive application in hot code. SPLIT is favored for diversity at near-zero cost, helping distinguish otherwise similar introsort instantiations. IBR and ICALL are moderate contributors — bogus branches thicken the CFG cheaply and indirect calls hinder cross-referencing, but both carry per-execution cost. IGV is kept lowest and risk-weighted: this benchmark has few globals, so its payoff is small and global-variable transformation carries the most subtle correctness risk for C++ statics; it remains enabled at reduced weight for incremental diversity rather than disabled.
